_source: Extracted Nov 1 2026 from the Figma region and country pages (scripts/extract-regions.mjs). Facts on France/Italy/USA pages written from memory (Oct 27); world and US-state pages from Wine Folly (Oct 31).

regions.name: ITALY
regions.description: Italy makes wine in all 20 of its regions, from hundreds of native grapes. Italian wine is made for the table: bright acid, built for food.

facts.label: THE LABEL NAMES
facts.value: Usually the place, not the grape

taste.line: Savory and food-friendly. Italian wine tastes best with a meal.

pairs.name: Short Rib
pairs.why: Bolgheri Rosso, from the Tuscan coast.

regions.sayIt: “Italian wines are made to go with food.”
regions.goodToKnow: DOCG is Italy’s top quality label. Look for the strip around the bottle’s neck.

regions.name: FRANCE
regions.description: France set the standard for wine. Its labels name the place, and each place has rules for which grapes can grow there.

taste.line: Elegant and balanced, with less ripe fruit than American wine.

pairs.name: Date Cake
pairs.why: Sauternes, a sweet white from Bordeaux.

regions.sayIt: “A French wine. It’s named for where it’s from, so let me tell you the grape.”
regions.goodToKnow: France’s AOC rules protect each place. They control the grapes, the yields and how the wine is made.

regions.name: USA
regions.description: American wine is usually labeled by grape, so it’s easy to read. California leads, with Oregon, Washington, New York and Michigan growing fast.

taste.line: Riper and fruitier than Europe, often with more oak.

pairs.name: Cauliflower
pairs.why: Michigan Riesling, or an unoaked Chardonnay.

regions.sayIt: “A California wine. Ripe, smooth and a little bolder than European wines.”
regions.goodToKnow: If a US label names a grape, at least 75% of the wine must be that grape.

regions.name: TUSCANY
regions.description: Rolling hills in central Italy and the home of Sangiovese. Chianti, Brunello, and the Bolgheri coast, where the Super Tuscans are made.

pairs.name: Short Rib
pairs.why: Our Bolgheri Rosso, from the Tuscan coast.

pairs.name: Mike’s Vegas Pie
pairs.why: A Chianti with cheese and sauce.

regions.sayIt: “Tuscany, the home of Chianti. Our Bolgheri Rosso comes from the Tuscan coast.”
regions.goodToKnow: “Super Tuscans” blend in French grapes like Cabernet. The first famous ones came from the Bolgheri coast.

regions.name: PIEDMONT
regions.description: Northwest Italy, at the foot of the Alps. Home of Nebbiolo, which makes Barolo and Barbaresco, and of easygoing Barbera.

taste.line: Perfumed, powerful reds. Barolo is called the “king of wines.”

regions.sayIt: “A wine from Piedmont, Barolo country. Perfumed and powerful.”
regions.goodToKnow: Agnolotti, the pasta on our menu, is a Piedmont specialty.

regions.name: VENETO
regions.description: Northeast Italy, around Venice and Verona. Makes Prosecco, crisp Soave and rich Amarone from dried grapes.

taste.line: From light bubbles to one of Italy’s richest reds.

regions.sayIt: “From the Veneto, near Venice. Home of Prosecco and Amarone.”
regions.goodToKnow: Amarone is made from grapes dried for months, which concentrates the flavor.

regions.name: SICILY
regions.description: Italy’s biggest island. Sun-ripened reds like Nero d’Avola, and fresh, mineral wines from the slopes of Mount Etna.

stats.lookFor: Nero d’Avola, Etna Rosso, Etna Bianco

facts.label: LOOK FOR
facts.value: Nero d’Avola, Etna Rosso, Etna Bianco

taste.line: Ripe reds and volcanic, mineral wines.

regions.sayIt: “A Sicilian wine. Ripe and sunny, from Italy’s biggest island.”
regions.goodToKnow: Arancini, like our Short Rib Arancini, come from Sicily.

regions.name: FRIULI
regions.description: The northeast corner of Italy, next to Slovenia. Known for crisp whites and some of the world’s most famous orange wines.

pairs.name: Walleye Milanese
pairs.why: A crisp white with crispy fish.

regions.sayIt: “A white from Friuli, in Italy’s northeast. Crisp and aromatic.”
regions.goodToKnow: Friuli’s Collio hills run straight across the border into Slovenia.

regions.name: BORDEAUX
regions.description: France’s most famous red wine region. Blends of Cabernet and Merlot, split by the river into the Left Bank and the Right Bank.

taste.line: Structured, elegant reds built to age.

pairs.name: Short Rib
pairs.why: A structured red with a rich braise.

regions.sayIt: “A Bordeaux. A Cabernet and Merlot blend, elegant and structured.”
regions.goodToKnow: Left Bank wines lean on Cabernet. Right Bank wines, like Pomerol, lean on Merlot.

regions.name: BURGUNDY
regions.description: A narrow strip of eastern France where Pinot Noir and Chardonnay grow in tiny vineyard plots. Labels name the village, or even the vineyard.

stats.lookFor: Chablis, Côte de Nuits, Côte de Beaune

facts.label: LOOK FOR
facts.value: Chablis, Côte de Nuits, Côte de Beaune

pairs.name: Scallop Rockefeller
pairs.why: White Burgundy with a rich topping.

regions.sayIt: “A Burgundy. Red Burgundy is Pinot Noir, white is Chardonnay.”
regions.goodToKnow: Red Burgundy is Pinot Noir. White Burgundy is Chardonnay.

regions.name: CHAMPAGNE
regions.description: Northeast of Paris and one of the coldest wine regions in France. Chalky soil and cool weather make the world’s most famous sparkling wine.
regions.sayIt: “A Champagne, from the region itself. Fine bubbles and toast.”
regions.goodToKnow: Blanc de Blancs is made only from white grapes. Blanc de Noirs is white wine from red grapes.

regions.name: RHÔNE
regions.description: The Rhône River valley in southeast France. Syrah in the north; Grenache blends like Châteauneuf-du-Pape in the south.

pairs.name: Short Rib
pairs.why: Peppery red with a rich braise.

pairs.name: Mike’s Vegas Pie
pairs.why: A Côtes du Rhône with a hearty pie.

regions.sayIt: “A Rhône red. Spicy and warming, with dark fruit.”
regions.goodToKnow: Châteauneuf-du-Pape allows up to 13 grape varieties in its blend.

regions.name: LOIRE
regions.description: France’s longest river, lined with châteaux and vineyards. Famous for crisp Sauvignon Blanc and Chenin Blanc.

pairs.name: Beet Confit
pairs.why: Zesty with crème fraîche and orange.

pairs.name: Scallop Rockefeller
pairs.why: A Vouvray with a rich topping.

regions.sayIt: “A Loire white. Crisp and mineral.”
regions.goodToKnow: Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé are both Sauvignon Blanc, from opposite banks of the Loire.

regions.name: PROVENCE
regions.description: The sunny south of France, on the Mediterranean. Most of its wine is pale, dry rosé.
regions.sayIt: “A Provence rosé. Pale, dry and crisp.”
regions.goodToKnow: Bandol, in Provence, is known for red and rosé made from Mourvèdre.

regions.name: NAPA VALLEY
regions.description: A small valley north of San Francisco and America’s most famous wine region. Known for rich, ripe Cabernet.

pairs.name: Short Rib
pairs.why: Napa Cabernet with a rich braise.

pairs.name: Scallop Rockefeller
pairs.why: Napa Chardonnay with a rich topping.

regions.sayIt: “A Napa Cabernet. Rich and ripe, with dark fruit.”
regions.goodToKnow: In 1976, Napa wines beat top French wines in a blind tasting known as the Judgment of Paris.

regions.name: SONOMA
regions.description: Napa’s bigger, more laid-back neighbor. Cool coastal spots grow Pinot Noir and Chardonnay; warm valleys grow Zinfandel.

stats.lookFor: Russian River Valley, Dry Creek, Sonoma Coast

facts.label: LOOK FOR
facts.value: Russian River Valley, Dry Creek, Sonoma Coast

taste.line: Lots of styles, all with ripe California fruit.

regions.sayIt: “A Sonoma wine. Ripe California fruit with a cooler, coastal edge.”
regions.goodToKnow: Sonoma County has more vineyard land than Napa.

regions.name: PASO ROBLES
regions.description: Halfway between San Francisco and Los Angeles, in San Luis Obispo County, just north of Santa Barbara. Hot days and cold nights make bold Cabernet, Zinfandel and Rhône-style blends.

stats.lookFor: Paso Robles, Adelaida District, Willow Creek

facts.label: LOOK FOR
facts.value: Paso Robles, Adelaida District, Willow Creek

pairs.name: Short Rib
pairs.why: Paso Cabernet or a Rhône-style blend.

regions.sayIt: “A Paso Robles red. Big and ripe, from California’s Central Coast.”
regions.goodToKnow: Paso Robles can swing 40–50°F between day and night, which keeps the grapes fresh.

regions.name: SANTA BARBARA
regions.description: Its mountains run east to west, so cold Pacific fog flows straight into the valleys. That makes some of California’s best cool-climate Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, especially from the Sta. Rita Hills.

stats.lookFor: Sta. Rita Hills, Santa Maria Valley, Santa Ynez Valley

facts.label: LOOK FOR
facts.value: Sta. Rita Hills, Santa Maria Valley, Santa Ynez Valley

taste.line: Bright and elegant, with California fruit.

pairs.name: Agnolotti
pairs.why: A Sta. Rita Hills Pinot Noir.

regions.sayIt: “A Santa Barbara Pinot. Bright and elegant, from the cool coast.”
regions.goodToKnow: Santa Barbara wine country was the setting of the 2004 movie Sideways.

regions.name: WILLAMETTE VALLEY
regions.description: Oregon’s main wine region, south of Portland. Its cool climate makes elegant Pinot Noir and crisp Pinot Gris.

taste.line: Elegant and earthy, closer to Burgundy than to California.

regions.sayIt: “An Oregon Pinot Noir. Elegant, with cherry and earth.”
regions.goodToKnow: Burgundy’s Drouhin family opened Domaine Drouhin Oregon in the Willamette Valley in the late 1980s.

regions.name: WASHINGTON
regions.description: Most vineyards sit east of the Cascade Mountains, in a dry, sunny desert. Known for Cabernet, Merlot, Syrah and Riesling.

stats.lookFor: Columbia Valley, Walla Walla, Red Mountain

facts.label: LOOK FOR
facts.value: Columbia Valley, Walla Walla, Red Mountain

regions.sayIt: “A Washington wine. Ripe fruit, with bright acid.”
regions.goodToKnow: Washington is the second-largest wine-producing state in the US, after California.

regions.name: MICHIGAN
regions.description: Northern Michigan’s peninsulas, near Traverse City. Lake Michigan keeps the vines mild, making crisp Riesling, sparkling wine and Pinot Noir.

taste.line: Crisp, bright and local. Guests love a Michigan wine.

regions.sayIt: “A Michigan wine, from up near Traverse City. Crisp and bright.”
regions.goodToKnow: Lake Michigan acts like a blanket, protecting the vines from early frost.

regions.name: TRENTINO-ALTO ADIGE
regions.description: Italy’s Alpine north, on the Austrian border. Crisp, clean whites from steep mountain vineyards, plus light reds.

taste.line: Clean, crisp whites with mountain freshness.

pairs.name: Scallops Rockefeller
pairs.why: A crisp Alpine white cuts the butter.

regions.sayIt: “From the Italian Alps: crisp, clean and refreshing.”
regions.goodToKnow: It’s bilingual. Many labels are in both Italian and German.

regions.name: LOMBARDY
regions.description: Milan’s region. Best known for Franciacorta, Italy’s answer to Champagne, made the same way in the bottle.

taste.line: Fine, toasty bubbles, like a softer Champagne.

regions.sayIt: “Italy’s Champagne-method sparkling, from near Milan.”
regions.goodToKnow: Franciacorta gets its bubbles the way Champagne does: a second fermentation in the bottle.

regions.name: EMILIA-ROMAGNA
regions.description: The food heart of Italy: Parmigiano, prosciutto di Parma and balsamic. The wine is Lambrusco, a fizzy red made for rich food.

taste.line: Fizzy, fruity reds that cut rich food.

pairs.name: Prosciutto Fondue
pairs.why: Lambrusco with ham and cheese, the classic.

pairs.name: Double Pepperoni Pizza
pairs.why: A chilled fizzy red with pizza.

regions.sayIt: “A fizzy red from the home of Parmigiano and prosciutto.”
regions.goodToKnow: Serve Lambrusco lightly chilled.

regions.name: MARCHE
regions.description: Central Italy on the Adriatic coast. Bright, crisp whites like Verdicchio, made for seafood.

stats.lookFor: Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi, Offida, Rosso Cònero

facts.label: LOOK FOR
facts.value: Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi, Offida, Rosso Cònero

taste.line: Crisp, salty whites with a bitter-almond finish.

pairs.name: Walleye Milanese
pairs.why: A coastal white for fried fish.

regions.sayIt: “Crisp whites from Italy’s Adriatic coast, made for seafood.”
regions.goodToKnow: Verdicchio means “little green”, for the green tint of the grape.

regions.name: UMBRIA
regions.description: Tuscany’s landlocked neighbour, “the green heart of Italy”. Orvieto whites and bold Sagrantino reds from Montefalco.

taste.line: Big, tannic reds and easygoing whites.

pairs.name: Rigatoni Ragu
pairs.why: Montefalco Rosso with a meat sauce.

regions.sayIt: “From the green heart of Italy, right next to Tuscany.”
regions.goodToKnow: Sagrantino is one of the most tannic grapes there is. It needs food.

regions.name: ABRUZZO
regions.description: Mountains down to the Adriatic in central Italy. Home of Montepulciano d’Abruzzo, a juicy, easy red and a great value.

taste.line: Juicy, everyday reds for pasta and pizza.

pairs.name: Sunday Sauce Pasta
pairs.why: A juicy red with red sauce.

regions.sayIt: “A juicy, easy red from Italy’s Adriatic side.”
regions.goodToKnow: Montepulciano d’Abruzzo is a grape. Vino Nobile di Montepulciano is a Tuscan town making Sangiovese. Different wines.

regions.name: CAMPANIA
regions.description: Naples and the Amalfi Coast. Volcanic soil from Vesuvius gives smoky Aglianico reds and fresh Fiano and Greco whites.

stats.lookFor: Taurasi, Fiano di Avellino, Greco di Tufo, Falanghina

facts.label: LOOK FOR
facts.value: Taurasi, Fiano di Avellino, Greco di Tufo, Falanghina

taste.line: Smoky, powerful reds and bright whites from volcanic soil.

pairs.name: Cali Margherita Pizza
pairs.why: A Campanian white with the pizza Naples made famous.

regions.sayIt: “From Naples and Vesuvius, the birthplace of pizza.”
regions.goodToKnow: Taurasi, made from Aglianico, is often called “the Barolo of the South”.

regions.name: PUGLIA
regions.description: The heel of Italy’s boot. Hot and sunny, making ripe, plush reds like Primitivo, the same grape as Zinfandel.

taste.line: Ripe, plush reds with soft tannins.

pairs.name: Rigatoni Ragu
pairs.why: A ripe red with a rich ragu.

regions.sayIt: “From the heel of Italy: ripe and smooth, Zinfandel’s Italian twin.”
regions.goodToKnow: Primitivo and Zinfandel are the same grape. DNA traced both to Croatia.

regions.name: SARDINIA
regions.description: An island west of mainland Italy. Cannonau, the local name for Grenache, and salty Vermentino whites.

stats.lookFor: Cannonau di Sardegna, Vermentino di Gallura

facts.label: LOOK FOR
facts.value: Cannonau di Sardegna, Vermentino di Gallura

taste.line: Sunny reds and salty, coastal whites.

regions.sayIt: “Island wines: sunny reds and salty whites from Sardinia.”
regions.goodToKnow: Cannonau is Sardinia’s name for Grenache.

regions.name: ALSACE
regions.description: On France’s border with Germany, sheltered by the Vosges mountains. Dry, aromatic whites, labelled by grape.

taste.line: Aromatic, dry whites full of fruit.

pairs.name: Harissa Carrots
pairs.why: An aromatic white with gentle spice.

pairs.name: Prosciutto Fondue
pairs.why: An Alsace white with melted cheese.

regions.sayIt: “French whites with German grapes, from the border with Germany.”
regions.goodToKnow: Alsace is one of the few French regions that puts the grape on the label.

regions.name: BEAUJOLAIS
regions.description: Just south of Burgundy. Light, juicy reds from Gamay, from easy Beaujolais to the serious cru villages.

taste.line: Light, juicy reds that like a slight chill.

pairs.name: Roasted Chicken
pairs.why: A light red with roast chicken.

regions.sayIt: “Light, juicy reds from just south of Burgundy.”
regions.goodToKnow: Beaujolais Nouveau is released on the third Thursday of November.

regions.name: LANGUEDOC-ROUSSILLON
regions.description: France’s big, sunny south coast between Provence and Spain. Generous blends of Grenache, Syrah and Mourvèdre.

pairs.name: Lamb Chops
pairs.why: A southern French red with lamb.

pairs.name: Baldwin Burger
pairs.why: An easy red with a burger.

regions.sayIt: “Sunny reds from France’s Mediterranean coast.”
regions.goodToKnow: Limoux, in the Languedoc, claims sparkling wine before Champagne.

regions.name: SOUTH WEST
regions.description: Inland from Bordeaux to the Pyrenees. Cahors, where Malbec comes from, plus Madiran and sweet Jurançon.

taste.line: Dark, firm reds with a rustic edge.

regions.sayIt: “Malbec’s original home, long before Argentina.”
regions.goodToKnow: Cahors Malbec is darker and firmer than most Argentine Malbec.

regions.name: JURA
regions.description: A small, cool region in the mountains near Switzerland. Unusual wines, like nutty vin jaune and pale, light reds.

stats.lookFor: Arbois, Côtes du Jura, Château-Chalon, Vin Jaune

facts.label: LOOK FOR
facts.value: Arbois, Côtes du Jura, Château-Chalon, Vin Jaune

taste.line: Nutty, savory wines unlike anything else.

pairs.name: Prosciutto Fondue
pairs.why: Jura wine and melted cheese, a local pairing.

pairs.name: Roasted Chicken
pairs.why: A Jura white with roast chicken.

regions.sayIt: “A rare mountain wine: nutty, savory and different.”
regions.goodToKnow: Vin jaune ages under a layer of yeast for over six years and comes in a 62 cl bottle called a clavelin.

regions.name: FINGER LAKES
regions.description: Upstate New York, around long, deep glacial lakes. Crisp, cool-climate Riesling and lighter reds.

stats.lookFor: Seneca Lake, Keuka Lake, dry Riesling

facts.label: LOOK FOR
facts.value: Seneca Lake, Keuka Lake, dry Riesling

regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN NEW YORK

taste.line: Bright, crisp Rieslings, dry to off-dry.

pairs.name: Walleye Milanese
pairs.why: Great Lakes fish, Finger Lakes Riesling.

pairs.name: Hot Honey Eggplant
pairs.why: An off-dry Riesling with sweet heat.

regions.sayIt: “Cool-climate Riesling from upstate New York.”
regions.goodToKnow: The deep lakes hold summer heat and protect the vines through the winter.

regions.name: MENDOCINO
regions.description: North of Sonoma, from the foggy coast to warm inland valleys. Known for Anderson Valley Pinot Noir and sparkling wine.

taste.line: Silky, cool-coast Pinot and fine sparkling.

regions.sayIt: “Cool-coast California Pinot, from north of Sonoma.”
regions.goodToKnow: Pacific fog runs up the Anderson Valley and keeps it cool.

regions.name: LODI
regions.description: Inland California, between San Francisco Bay and the Sierra. Known for old-vine Zinfandel, some vines over 100 years old.
regions.sayIt: “California’s old-vine Zinfandel country.”
regions.goodToKnow: “Old vine” has no legal meaning in the US. Each winery decides.

regions.name: VIRGINIA
regions.description: Historic East Coast wine country, where Thomas Jefferson planted vines. Cabernet Franc and Viognier do especially well.

taste.line: Herbal reds and floral, peachy whites.

regions.sayIt: “East Coast wine with history: Jefferson planted vines here.”
regions.goodToKnow: Viognier is Virginia’s official state grape.

regions.name: TEXAS HILL COUNTRY
regions.description: Central Texas, west of Austin. Heat-loving grapes from Spain, Italy and the Rhône do well here.

stats.lookFor: Texas Hill Country, Texas High Plains

facts.label: LOOK FOR
facts.value: Texas Hill Country, Texas High Plains

taste.line: Warm-climate reds from Spanish and Rhône grapes.

regions.sayIt: “Texas wine from the Hill Country, west of Austin.”
regions.goodToKnow: Many Hill Country wineries buy their grapes from the Texas High Plains, near Lubbock.

regions.name: SOUTHERN OREGON
regions.description: South of the Willamette, warmer and sunnier. The Umpqua, Rogue and Applegate valleys grow Syrah, Tempranillo and Pinot Noir.

stats.lookFor: Umpqua Valley, Rogue Valley, Applegate Valley

facts.label: LOOK FOR
facts.value: Umpqua Valley, Rogue Valley, Applegate Valley

taste.line: Riper, spicier reds than the Willamette.

regions.sayIt: “Sunnier Oregon: Syrah and Tempranillo from the Umpqua and Rogue valleys.”
regions.goodToKnow: Abacela, in the Umpqua Valley, planted the Pacific Northwest’s first Tempranillo in 1995.

regions.name: LONG ISLAND
regions.description: The east end of Long Island, New York, between the Atlantic and Long Island Sound. A maritime climate suited to Merlot, Cabernet Franc and crisp whites.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN NEW YORK

taste.line: Medium-bodied, Bordeaux-style reds and bright whites.

pairs.name: Roasted Chicken
pairs.why: Long Island Merlot with roast chicken.

pairs.name: Scallops Rockefeller
pairs.why: A crisp Long Island white with scallops.

regions.sayIt: “New York wine from the North Fork and the Hamptons.”
regions.goodToKnow: Long Island’s first modern vineyard was planted on the North Fork in 1973.

regions.name: ARIZONA
regions.description: High-elevation desert vineyards in southern and central Arizona. Warm days and cold nights grow Rhône, Spanish and Italian grapes.

taste.line: Sun-ripened reds kept fresh by cold nights.

regions.sayIt: “Desert wine from high up: warm days, cold nights.”
regions.goodToKnow: Sonoita became Arizona’s first wine region (AVA) in 1984.

regions.name: HOWELL MOUNTAIN
regions.description: Wooded mountain vineyards around Angwin, northeast of St. Helena. Some of Napa’s biggest, most age-worthy, high-tannin Cabernet.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN NAPA VALLEY
regions.sayIt: “Napa mountain Cabernet: big, powerful and built to age.”
regions.goodToKnow: Howell Mountain was Napa Valley’s first sub-AVA, in 1983.

regions.name: CARNEROS
regions.description: Straddles the south ends of Napa and Sonoma, cooled by breezes off San Pablo Bay. Shallow clay soils give structured Pinot Noir with good acidity.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN NAPA VALLEY
regions.sayIt: “Cool Napa and Sonoma Pinot and Chardonnay, by the bay.”
regions.goodToKnow: The shallow clay makes the vines work harder, which gives good acidity and aging potential.

regions.name: RUSSIAN RIVER VALLEY
regions.description: Rolling hills along the Russian River in central Sonoma. Its Pinot Noir is lighter in colour, velvety and high in acidity.
regions.sayIt: “Sonoma’s velvety, fog-cooled Pinot Noir.”
regions.goodToKnow: It’s known for sandy-loam soils called Goldridge and Franciscan.

regions.name: SONOMA COAST
regions.description: A remote, fog-covered coast making elegant Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. A few flagship wineries lead the way.
regions.sayIt: “Sonoma’s wild, foggy coast, made for Pinot Noir.”
regions.goodToKnow: It’s Sonoma County’s largest AVA, set up in 1987.

regions.name: DRY CREEK VALLEY
regions.description: A Sonoma valley known for rich, full-bodied reds, Zinfandel above all.

pairs.name: Baldwin Burger
pairs.why: Dry Creek Zin with a burger.

regions.sayIt: “Sonoma’s Zinfandel valley.”
regions.goodToKnow: About 10,000 acres of vines. An AVA since 1983.

regions.name: CALIFORNIA
regions.description: Wine here began about 240 years ago at the San Diego mission and spread to Sonoma and Napa after the 1849 gold rush. California now makes 80% of US wine.
regions.sayIt: “California makes 80% of America’s wine.”
regions.goodToKnow: At the 1976 Judgment of Paris blind tasting, two Napa wines scored top against Bordeaux.

regions.name: ALEXANDER VALLEY
regions.description: A Sonoma valley for rich, full-bodied reds: Cabernet, hillside Merlot and richly flavoured Chardonnay.
regions.sayIt: “Sonoma’s rich Cabernet valley.”
regions.goodToKnow: Volcanic soil from an ancient eruption of Mount St. Helena filled the valley.

regions.name: LAKE COUNTY
regions.description: Just north of Napa, around Clear Lake and Mount Konocti. Volcanic soils give bold, “dusty” reds in a Napa-like style.

taste.line: Bold, dusty reds from volcanic soil.

pairs.name: Braised Short Rib
pairs.why: Lake County Cab with braised beef.

pairs.name: Baldwin Burger
pairs.why: A bold red with a burger.

regions.sayIt: “Napa-style reds from volcanic soil, just to the north.”
regions.goodToKnow: Clear Lake is a natural lake about 480,000 years old.

regions.name: OAKVILLE
regions.description: A Napa Valley floor region, a little warmer than Yountville, and home to some of Napa’s most famous Cabernet vineyards.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN NAPA VALLEY
regions.sayIt: “The heart of Napa’s valley floor, famous for Cabernet.”
regions.goodToKnow: Oakville became its own AVA in 1993. To Kalon, Harlan Estate and Screaming Eagle are all here.

regions.name: SANTA CRUZ MOUNTAINS
regions.description: Mountain vineyards between Monterey Bay and San Francisco, some up to 2,800 ft. Mineral, complex Pinot Noir with the tannin to age.

taste.line: Mineral, complex wines built to age.

regions.sayIt: “Mountain wine between San Francisco and Monterey Bay.”
regions.goodToKnow: Some vineyards here reach 2,800 feet.

regions.name: SANTA LUCIA HIGHLANDS
regions.description: Vineyards on the eastern ridge of the Santa Lucia Mountains, south of Monterey Bay. Lush but complex Pinot with black cherry, rose and dusty minerality.
regions.sayIt: “Monterey Pinot from a windy mountain ridge.”
regions.goodToKnow: Near-constant winds stretch the growing season.

regions.name: EDNA VALLEY
regions.description: Near San Luis Obispo, one of the SLO Coast’s two AVAs with Arroyo Grande Valley. Rich Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.

taste.line: Rich Chardonnay and Pinot from the cool coast.

regions.sayIt: “Cool-coast Chardonnay from near San Luis Obispo.”
regions.goodToKnow: Edna Valley and Arroyo Grande Valley are the two AVAs on the SLO Coast.

regions.name: SIERRA FOOTHILLS
regions.description: High vineyards around the gold-rush towns of Murphys, Plymouth and Placerville. Independent winemakers working with Zinfandel, Syrah and lesser-known grapes.

taste.line: Bold, spicy reds from Gold Country.

regions.sayIt: “Gold Rush country wine, high in the Sierra foothills.”
regions.goodToKnow: Winemakers are moving here for organic, biodynamic and even vegan winemaking.

regions.name: STA. RITA HILLS
regions.description: Between Buellton and Lompoc. An east-west valley funnels in sea breezes and fog for elegant, structured Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN SANTA BARBARA
regions.sayIt: “Cool Santa Barbara Pinot, shaped by the sea breeze.”
regions.goodToKnow: The “Sta.” spelling came from a legal dispute with Chile’s Santa Rita winery.

regions.name: SANTA MARIA VALLEY
regions.description: A funnel-shaped valley and Santa Barbara’s first AVA (1981), the first in the county planted to Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN SANTA BARBARA

taste.line: Bright Chardonnay and Pinot from a long, cool season.

regions.sayIt: “Santa Barbara’s first wine region.”
regions.goodToKnow: Home to Bien Nacido, a famous 900-acre vineyard.

regions.name: SANTA YNEZ VALLEY
regions.description: Santa Barbara’s largest AVA. Foggy Pinot and Chardonnay country in the west, warm Rhône and Bordeaux grapes in the east.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN SANTA BARBARA

taste.line: Everything from cool Pinot to warm Syrah.

regions.sayIt: “Santa Barbara’s biggest valley: over 60 grapes.”
regions.goodToKnow: It runs more than 30 miles east to west and grows over 60 grape varieties.

regions.name: RUTHERFORD
regions.description: A Napa Valley floor region known for expressive Cabernet Sauvignon. Wine Folly’s warning: it gets expensive.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN NAPA VALLEY
regions.sayIt: “Valley-floor Napa Cabernet, full of character.”
regions.goodToKnow: Rutherford became its own AVA in 1993.

regions.name: STAGS LEAP DISTRICT
regions.description: On Napa’s east side, below the Stags Leap Palisades. Famous for inky Cabernet that tastes rich, lush and opulent.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN NAPA VALLEY
regions.sayIt: “The Napa Cabernet that beat France in 1976.”
regions.goodToKnow: Stag’s Leap Wine Cellars’ 1973 Cabernet won the 1976 Judgment of Paris blind tasting.

regions.name: YAMHILL-CARLTON
regions.description: Low, rolling hills southwest of Ribbon Ridge that stay warm later into the afternoon. Fruit-forward Pinot with black cherry and vanilla.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN WILLAMETTE VALLEY
regions.sayIt: “Juicy, fruit-forward Oregon Pinot.”
regions.goodToKnow: It’s spread out, with miles of driving between vineyards.

regions.name: RIBBON RIDGE
regions.description: A small ridge inside the Chehalem Mountains. Intense cranberry and rustic, earthy Pinot, the classic Oregon style.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN WILLAMETTE VALLEY
regions.sayIt: “Classic, earthy Oregon Pinot from a tiny ridge.”
regions.goodToKnow: It earned its own AVA even though it sits inside the Chehalem Mountains.

regions.name: MCMINNVILLE
regions.description: Named for the town. South-facing vineyards make rich dark-cherry and plum Pinot, some rustic with pine and herb notes.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN WILLAMETTE VALLEY

taste.line: Dark-fruited Pinot with a rustic edge.

regions.sayIt: “Dark-fruited Oregon Pinot from McMinnville.”
regions.goodToKnow: The angle of the slope changes the flavour a lot here.

regions.name: OREGON
regions.description: Most vineyards are in the northern Willamette Valley, first planted with Burgundy grapes in the 1960s. Small wineries and strict standards make tart-fruited, subtle, elegant wines.
regions.sayIt: “Oregon: small wineries and elegant Pinot Noir.”
regions.goodToKnow: A wine labelled with a grape in Oregon must be at least 90% that grape.

regions.name: COLUMBIA GORGE
regions.description: On the Oregon-Washington border, an outdoor-adventure wine trip with a handful of pioneering wineries. Rhône-style reds, and whites from the Klickitat area.

pairs.name: Harissa Carrots
pairs.why: A Rhône-style red with gentle spice.

regions.sayIt: “Wine and adventure in the Columbia River Gorge.”
regions.goodToKnow: Come for the wine, stay for biking, kite surfing, hiking and fishing.

regions.name: COLUMBIA VALLEY
regions.description: Washington’s biggest AVA, with 99% of the state’s vineyards on the dry, sunny east side. Bold, fruit-forward reds at good values.

stats.climate: About 300 days of sun, very dry

facts.label: CLIMATE
facts.value: About 300 days of sun, very dry

taste.line: Bold, fruit-forward reds with sweet-tart acidity.

regions.sayIt: “Sunny, bold reds from eastern Washington.”
regions.goodToKnow: It gets about as little rain as the Gobi Desert.

regions.name: WALLA WALLA VALLEY
regions.description: A small region on the Oregon-Washington border with some of the best Syrah in the US. Cabernet is the most planted grape.

pairs.name: Baldwin Burger
pairs.why: A rich red with a burger.

regions.sayIt: “Some of America’s best Syrah, on the Oregon border.”
regions.goodToKnow: When it became an AVA in 1984, only 60 acres were planted.

regions.name: YAKIMA VALLEY
regions.description: A varied valley making a wide range of reds and whites. Red Mountain, Snipes Mountain and Rattlesnake Hills sit inside it.

taste.line: A wide range of reds and whites.

regions.sayIt: “The Pacific Northwest’s oldest wine region.”
regions.goodToKnow: Set up in 1983, it’s the Pacific Northwest’s oldest AVA.

regions.name: DUNDEE HILLS
regions.description: Some of Oregon’s oldest vineyards, in a tight cluster of growers. Pinot Noir with raspberry and black tea, plus Chardonnay and sparkling.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN WILLAMETTE VALLEY

taste.line: Pinot with raspberry and black tea.

regions.sayIt: “Oregon’s classic Pinot hills.”
regions.goodToKnow: Eyrie Vineyards planted here first, in 1965.

regions.name: RED MOUNTAIN
regions.description: A tiny region making dark, tannic, acclaimed reds, in one of Washington’s hottest spots.

pairs.name: Braised Short Rib
pairs.why: A powerful red with braised beef.

regions.sayIt: “Small, hot and famous for powerful Cabernet.”
regions.goodToKnow: Its whites, like Chenin Blanc, tend to be low in acidity.

regions.name: HORSE HEAVEN HILLS
regions.description: A wide, empty landscape of huge vineyards known for quantity and quality.
regions.sayIt: “Home to Washington’s first 100-point wines.”
regions.goodToKnow: Quilceda Creek made Washington’s first three 100-point wines here, from old vines at Champoux Vineyard.

regions.name: WAHLUKE SLOPE
regions.description: A quiet, remote region making consistently great reds at fair prices.

taste.line: Consistent, ripe reds at fair prices.

pairs.name: Baldwin Burger
pairs.why: A ripe red with a burger.

regions.sayIt: “Washington value: ripe reds at fair prices.”
regions.goodToKnow: Wine Folly lists it among the Columbia Valley’s best-value regions.

regions.name: LAKE CHELAN
regions.description: A sunny getaway for Seattle around a glacier-fed lake. Known for sparkling and aromatic whites as well as reds.

stats.climate: The lake evens out heat and cold

facts.label: CLIMATE
facts.value: The lake evens out heat and cold

taste.line: Fresh, bright wines from a lakeside region.

regions.sayIt: “Lakeside wine, a favourite getaway from Seattle.”
regions.goodToKnow: The lake protects the vines from extreme heat and cold.

regions.name: NEW YORK
regions.description: America’s third-largest wine state. Its fine wine comes from the Finger Lakes, Long Island, Lake Erie and the Hudson River.

stats.climate: Cold upstate, maritime on Long Island
stats.lookFor: Finger Lakes, Long Island, Hudson River

facts.label: CLIMATE
facts.value: Cold upstate, maritime on Long Island

facts.label: LOOK FOR
facts.value: Finger Lakes, Long Island, Hudson River

taste.line: Crisp whites and fresh, lighter reds.

pairs.name: Walleye Milanese
pairs.why: New York Riesling with Great Lakes fish.

regions.sayIt: “From the Finger Lakes to Long Island.”
regions.goodToKnow: New York has America’s first bonded winery (Pleasant Valley) and its oldest working winery (Brotherhood).

regions.name: HUDSON RIVER REGION
regions.description: Close to New York City, with 300+ years of grape growing. Now a hot spot for Cabernet Franc, with historic hybrids like Seyval Blanc and Baco Noir.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN NEW YORK

taste.line: Fresh, herbal reds and crisp whites.

regions.sayIt: “Wine from just up the river from New York City.”
regions.goodToKnow: It was New York’s first AVA, in 1982. French Huguenots planted vines here in the late 1600s.

regions.name: OLD MISSION PENINSULA
regions.description: A slender 19-mile peninsula into Grand Traverse Bay, with water on three sides. Riesling in every style, bone dry to ice wine and sparkling.

stats.climate: Water on three sides, long autumns

facts.label: CLIMATE
facts.value: Water on three sides, long autumns

taste.line: Riesling every way, dry to sweet.

pairs.name: Walleye Milanese
pairs.why: Michigan Riesling with Great Lakes fish.

pairs.name: Hot Honey Eggplant
pairs.why: An off-dry Riesling with sweet heat.

regions.sayIt: “Michigan Riesling from a peninsula in Grand Traverse Bay.”
regions.goodToKnow: It’s named for a Presbyterian mission founded in 1842.

regions.name: LEELANAU PENINSULA
regions.description: A cool-climate region in northwest Michigan on glacial soils. Vibrant Riesling, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, with Gamay a rising star.
regions.sayIt: “Cool-climate Michigan wine on the 45th parallel.”
regions.goodToKnow: It sits at 45°N, the same latitude as Bordeaux.

regions.name: TEXAS HIGH PLAINS
regions.description: A high, dry plateau in the Texas Panhandle that grows the grapes for many Hill Country wineries.

stats.climate: Higher, cooler, drier than Hill Country

facts.label: CLIMATE
facts.value: Higher, cooler, drier than Hill Country

taste.line: Ripe reds from high, sunny vineyards.

pairs.name: Smash Burger
pairs.why: A ripe red with a burger.

regions.sayIt: “Texas’s vineyard country, up in the Panhandle.”
regions.goodToKnow: Hill Country tasting rooms pour both Hill Country and High Plains wines.

regions.name: SNAKE RIVER VALLEY
regions.description: Idaho’s largest wine region, across southwest Idaho into Oregon. High desert gives ripe reds and fresh, elegant whites.

taste.line: Ripe reds and fresh, elegant whites.

regions.sayIt: “Idaho wine from the high desert.”
regions.goodToKnow: Vineyards sit at 2,500–3,000 feet, over 400 miles from the Pacific.

regions.name: EOLA-AMITY HILLS
regions.description: Low hills running south toward Salem. The best vineyards face southeast, and the Pinot shows rich plum, currant and subtle five-spice.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN WILLAMETTE VALLEY

taste.line: Rich Pinot with plum and spice.

regions.sayIt: “Oregon Pinot with plum and spice, near Salem.”
regions.goodToKnow: The best vineyards face southeast, along Highway 221.

regions.name: CHEHALEM MOUNTAINS
regions.description: Hills southwest of Portland, growing fast for being close to the city. Some of Oregon’s bolder Pinot Noir: cherry, black tea and cinnamon.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN WILLAMETTE VALLEY

taste.line: Bolder Pinot with cherry and spice.

regions.sayIt: “Bolder Oregon Pinot, close to Portland.”
regions.goodToKnow: It’s the first wine region you reach flying into Portland.

regions.name: GREECE
regions.description: One of the oldest winemaking places on earth, growing mostly native grapes. Its wines match the intensity of Greek food.

facts.label: CLIMATE
facts.value: Cooler north, hot south and islands

regions.sayIt: “Greece: some of the oldest wine on earth, made for food.”
regions.goodToKnow: Limnio, a red from Lemnos, is thought to be mentioned in Aristotle’s writings.

regions.name: HUNGARY
regions.description: 22 wine regions making dry whites, fine reds and legendary sweet Tokaji, in a renaissance that mixes tradition with modern winemaking.

taste.line: Dry whites and legendary sweet wine.

regions.sayIt: “Hungary: home of Tokaji, the legendary sweet wine.”
regions.goodToKnow: In the 1700s, Tokaji Aszú was the most sought-after dessert wine in the world.

regions.name: GEORGIA
regions.description: Best known for qvevri wines, fermented in big clay vessels buried underground. Long skin contact gives tannin, texture and earthy, savory flavour.
regions.sayIt: “Georgia: 8,000 years of wine, made in clay.”
regions.goodToKnow: Winemaking in Georgia dates to about 6000 BC.

regions.name: ARGENTINA
regions.description: One of the world’s biggest wine producers. Most vineyards sit at the foot of the Andes, where sun and snowmelt give plump, deep-coloured wines. Malbec leads.
regions.sayIt: “Argentina: Malbec from the foot of the Andes.”
regions.goodToKnow: Vineyards reach above 7,500 ft, and the cool nights up there keep the wines fresh.

regions.name: CHILE
regions.description: A thin strip between the Pacific and the Andes. Early French investment brought Bordeaux grapes, and much of its “Merlot” turned out to be Carménère.

taste.line: Bordeaux grapes with a Chilean accent.

regions.sayIt: “Chile: Bordeaux grapes between the Andes and the Pacific.”
regions.goodToKnow: Chile’s vineyards have never been hit by phylloxera.

regions.name: AUSTRALIA
regions.description: Nearly 340,000 acres of vines, known above all for Shiraz, and an industry that keeps innovating.

facts.label: FAMOUS REGIONS
facts.value: Barossa Valley, Margaret River, Yarra Valley

taste.line: Bold, ripe Shiraz and much more.

regions.sayIt: “Australia: big Shiraz, and a lot more.”
regions.goodToKnow: Nearly all Australian wine, even top bottles, is sealed with a screw cap.

regions.name: SPAIN
regions.description: Every part of Spain makes wine, from the Atlantic and Mediterranean coasts to dry plateaus and the Pyrenees. Its wines sit between Old and New World: bold fruit with dusty minerality.

taste.line: Bold fruit with a dusty, old-world edge.

pairs.name: Prosciutto Fondue
pairs.why: A dry Sherry with ham and cheese.

regions.sayIt: “Spain: bold fruit with a dusty, old-world edge.”
regions.goodToKnow: Spain has the most vineyard land in the world but low yields: vines are planted far apart and use little water.

regions.name: NEW ZEALAND
regions.description: Ten wine regions across its islands. Called the Sauvignon Blanc capital of the world, and strong in cool-climate grapes.

facts.label: KEY GRAPES
facts.value: Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Riesling

taste.line: Zesty Sauvignon Blanc and cool-climate Pinot.

regions.sayIt: “New Zealand: the Sauvignon Blanc capital of the world.”
regions.goodToKnow: 98% of New Zealand’s vineyards meet the ISO 14001 sustainability standard.

regions.name: PORTUGAL
regions.description: A huge range of native grapes little known abroad, plus long traditions, so Portugal is strong on quality and value. Best known for Port, Madeira and Douro reds.

facts.label: KEY GRAPES
facts.value: Touriga Nacional, Alicante Bouschet, Arinto, Alvarinho

facts.label: CLIMATE
facts.value: Cool, wet north; hot inland Douro

pairs.name: Braised Short Rib
pairs.why: A Douro red with braised beef.

regions.sayIt: “Portugal: native grapes and great value, from Vinho Verde to Port.”
regions.goodToKnow: Port has been a demarcated region since 1757, one of the first in the world.

regions.name: SOUTH AFRICA
regions.description: Where Old World and New World meet. A warm climate and granite soils over 600 million years old give bold, aromatic reds and whites.

facts.label: KEY GRAPES
facts.value: Chenin Blanc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinotage, Syrah

pairs.name: Lamb Chops
pairs.why: A South African Syrah with lamb.

regions.sayIt: “South Africa: Old World meets New, on ancient granite.”
regions.goodToKnow: “Estate Wines” come from registered vineyards farmed as one unit. There are 207.

regions.name: GERMANY
regions.description: The world’s top Riesling producer, making it from dry to very sweet across 13 regions. The cool climate also suits light reds and aromatic whites.

taste.line: Riesling, from bone dry to very sweet.

pairs.name: Hot Honey Eggplant
pairs.why: An off-dry Riesling with sweet heat.

pairs.name: Walleye Milanese
pairs.why: A dry Riesling with fried fish.

regions.sayIt: “Germany: the home of Riesling, dry to sweet.”
regions.goodToKnow: Germany’s single-grape focus began with mass plantings of Riesling at Schloss Johannisberg in 1720.

regions.name: AUSTRIA
regions.description: Best known for Grüner Veltliner and its sharp, spicy whites. Austria rebuilt its wine industry after a 1985 scandal, with some of the strictest rules in wine.
regions.sayIt: “Austria: Grüner Veltliner, sharp and spicy.”
regions.goodToKnow: After the 1985 scandal, Austria adopted some of the strictest quality and labelling rules in wine.

regions.name: JEREZ
regions.description: Sherry is a fortified white wine from Andalucía, and most of it is dry. True Sherry comes only from the triangle of Jerez, Sanlúcar and El Puerto de Santa María.
regions.sayIt: “Sherry: Spain’s fortified wine, and most of it is dry.”
regions.goodToKnow: In 1587, Sir Francis Drake seized thousands of barrels of Sherry in Cádiz and started a Sherry craze in England.

regions.name: PENEDÈS
regions.description: Home of most Cava, Spain’s sparkling wine. It’s made the same way as Champagne but with Spanish grapes, and tastes lean, citrusy and savory.
regions.sayIt: “Cava: made like Champagne, with Spanish grapes.”
regions.goodToKnow: About 95% of Cava comes from around Penedès. The first was made in 1872.

regions.name: RUEDA
regions.description: Flat high plains south of Valladolid, home of the native white grape Verdejo. Wines labelled Rueda Verdejo must be at least 85% Verdejo.

pairs.name: Walleye Milanese
pairs.why: A crisp white with fried fish.

regions.sayIt: “Rueda: Spain’s crisp Verdejo.”
regions.goodToKnow: Sandy soils kept out phylloxera, so some Verdejo vines are over 100 years old.

regions.name: RIOJA
regions.description: In the Ebro River valley in northern Spain. Seven small side valleys create different terroirs, which is why Rioja varies so much in style.
regions.sayIt: “Rioja: Spain’s classic Tempranillo, from the Ebro valley.”
regions.goodToKnow: Rioja’s small valleys hold about 36% of Spain’s biodiversity.

regions.name: TORO
regions.description: Toro makes the most tannic but expressive style of Tempranillo, wines that age for many years.
regions.sayIt: “Toro: big, tannic Tempranillo that ages for years.”
regions.goodToKnow: Top bottles hit their best after about 12 years.

regions.name: DOURO
regions.description: The river valley where Port is made: a fortified wine in red, white and rosé, from dry to very sweet. Real Port only comes from the Douro.

pairs.name: Braised Short Rib
pairs.why: A Douro red with short rib.

regions.sayIt: “The Douro: home of Port and bold dry reds.”
regions.goodToKnow: Port uses at least 52 grape varieties, and top Vintage Port can age 100 years or more.

regions.name: VINHO VERDE
regions.description: Portugal’s cool Atlantic north, known for naturally low-alcohol whites from native grapes.
regions.sayIt: “Vinho Verde: light, fresh and low in alcohol.”
regions.goodToKnow: Traditional Vinho Verde is often just 8.5–10.5% alcohol.

regions.name: RIBERA DEL DUERO
regions.description: Tempranillo takes on a bolder style in the Duero River valley. Some of Spain’s most famous wineries are here, but good bottles still cost around $20.
regions.sayIt: “Bolder Tempranillo from the Duero valley.”
regions.goodToKnow: The Duero is the same river that flows on into Portugal’s Port country.

regions.name: ALENTEJO
regions.description: Possibly Europe’s last wild wine frontier. It never planted international grapes, so it now specializes in rare native ones.

taste.line: Ripe, bold wines from native grapes.

regions.sayIt: “Alentejo: Portugal’s wild south, all native grapes.”
regions.goodToKnow: Antão Vaz gets richer when made in a talha, a clay amphora.

regions.name: DÃO
regions.description: High vineyards on granite and schist. Lighter than the Douro, but the wines age well as tannin and acidity develop.

pairs.name: Roasted Chicken
pairs.why: A Dão red with roast chicken.

regions.sayIt: “Dão: Portugal’s elegant, age-worthy reds.”
regions.goodToKnow: Jaen, a Dão grape, is the same as Spain’s Mencía.

regions.name: MADEIRA
regions.description: A fortified wine from an Atlantic island, dry to sweet. Heating the wine again and again gives roasted-nut, caramel and toffee flavours.
regions.sayIt: “Madeira: island wine that can age a century.”
regions.goodToKnow: It began as wine aged in ships’ holds crossing the tropics.

regions.name: BAIRRADA
regions.description: Home of Baga, once known for dense, high-acid reds. Modern winemaking now makes lighter reds and sparkling wines too.
regions.sayIt: “Bairrada: Portugal’s Baga reds and sparkling.”
regions.goodToKnow: Top Baga wines keep improving for 10 to 20 years.

regions.name: MOSEL
regions.description: A winding river valley with extremely steep vineyards that makes the most classic Rieslings in the world. Nearly 90% of the vines are white grapes.

pairs.name: Hot Honey Eggplant
pairs.why: An off-dry Mosel Riesling with sweet heat.

regions.sayIt: “Mosel: the classic Riesling, from very steep slopes.”
regions.goodToKnow: The Calmont vineyard near Bremm is said to be Europe’s steepest, at about 68°.

regions.name: WACHAU
regions.description: A 12-mile, UNESCO-listed stretch of the Danube with steep stone terraces, planted mainly to Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
regions.sayIt: “Wachau: Austria’s Danube terraces.”
regions.goodToKnow: Nikolaihof is Austria’s oldest winery, with records back to 777.

regions.name: SANTORINI
regions.description: The birthplace and best region of Assyrtiko: lean whites with flint, lemon and a salty finish. The island also makes Vinsanto, a sun-dried sweet wine.
regions.sayIt: “Santorini Assyrtiko: lemon, flint and sea salt.”
regions.goodToKnow: Vinsanto smells like a red wine, even though it’s made from white grapes.

regions.name: NAOUSSA
regions.description: Xinomavro with high tannin and acidity, and dark cherry, licorice and spice. Limestone-rich soils add structure, so the wines age well.

taste.line: Structured reds, like a Greek Barolo.

regions.sayIt: “Naoussa Xinomavro: the Barolo of Greece.”
regions.goodToKnow: Xinomavro is called the Barolo of Greece because it can taste a lot like Nebbiolo.

regions.name: NEMEA
regions.description: In the Peloponnese, famous for Agiorgitiko: full-bodied, fruity reds with raspberry, plum and nutmeg and smooth tannins.
regions.sayIt: “Nemea: smooth, fruity Greek reds.”
regions.goodToKnow: Agiorgitiko is like Merlot with a bit more spice.

regions.name: TOKAJ
regions.description: Famous for sweet Aszú wines, plus dry Furmint and Eszencia, the world’s sweetest wine. Volcanic soils, rivers and mountains bring the noble rot.

taste.line: Sweet and dry wines with bright acidity.

regions.sayIt: “Tokaj: the world’s first classified wine region.”
regions.goodToKnow: Tokaj was classified in 1737, the first wine region in the world to be.

regions.name: PRIORAT
regions.description: A tiny, rugged region just south of Barcelona known for bold, powerful reds. It nearly disappeared by the 1970s and was revived from 1989.

pairs.name: Braised Short Rib
pairs.why: A powerful red with short rib.

regions.sayIt: “Powerful Spanish reds from steep slate hills near Barcelona.”
regions.goodToKnow: Winemaking here goes back to a priory founded in 1163.

regions.name: RÍAS BAIXAS
regions.description: In rainy Galicia, Spain’s Atlantic northwest. Five sub-zones share sandy granite soils, and strict rules cover grapes, yields and winemaking.

stats.lookFor: Rías Baixas Albariño, Val do Salnés

facts.label: LOOK FOR
facts.value: Rías Baixas Albariño, Val do Salnés

regions.sayIt: “Albariño from Spain’s Atlantic coast: fresh, salty, made for seafood.”
regions.goodToKnow: A tasting committee checks every wine; only those that pass can say Rías Baixas.

regions.name: MAIPO VALLEY
regions.description: Follows the Maipo river south of Santiago. Alto Maipo, at the foot of the Andes, makes full-bodied red blends that recall Napa Cabernet.
regions.sayIt: “Maipo: Chile’s Napa-style Cabernet.”
regions.goodToKnow: Viña Carmen made the first single-varietal Carménère.

regions.name: COLCHAGUA VALLEY
regions.description: Prime Bordeaux-grape vineyards from San Fernando to Santa Cruz. Its Apalta area is known for age-worthy Bordeaux-style blends.

pairs.name: Braised Short Rib
pairs.why: A Colchagua blend with short rib.

regions.sayIt: “Colchagua: Chile’s Carménère and Bordeaux blends.”
regions.goodToKnow: Casa Silva keeps its own Carménère clone garden.

regions.name: ACONCAGUA
regions.description: From the coast inland. Around Llay Lay, San Felipe and Los Andes it makes some of Chile’s most structured, tannic reds.

stats.climate: Very sunny and dry, cool nights

facts.label: CLIMATE
facts.value: Very sunny and dry, cool nights

pairs.name: Braised Short Rib
pairs.why: A structured red with short rib.

regions.sayIt: “Aconcagua: Chile’s sunniest, most structured reds.”
regions.goodToKnow: The reds often show red pepper, paprika and black tea notes.

regions.name: MENDOZA
regions.description: Argentina’s largest wine region, with 75% of the country’s vineyards. Hot, sunny and very dry in the shadow of the Andes, ideal for bold reds.

stats.climate: Hot, sunny, under 9 in. of rain
stats.lookFor: Mendoza, Uco Valley, Luján de Cuyo

facts.label: CLIMATE
facts.value: Hot, sunny, under 9 in. of rain

facts.label: LOOK FOR
facts.value: Mendoza, Uco Valley, Luján de Cuyo

regions.sayIt: “Mendoza: more Malbec than anywhere on earth.”
regions.goodToKnow: More Malbec is planted in Mendoza than anywhere else in the world.

regions.name: BAROSSA VALLEY
regions.description: One of Australia’s oldest and best-known regions. Its Shiraz is among the most powerful in the world: ripe blackberry, dried currant, mocha and tobacco.
regions.sayIt: “Barossa: some of the most powerful Shiraz in the world.”
regions.goodToKnow: Barossa has Shiraz vines over 100 years old.

regions.name: EDEN VALLEY
regions.description: Part of Barossa, higher in the hills. The elevation gives tart, high-acid, age-worthy wines and much of Barossa’s white wine.

stats.climate: Cooler and higher than Barossa Valley

facts.label: CLIMATE
facts.value: Cooler and higher than Barossa Valley

regions.sayIt: “Eden Valley: Barossa’s cool hills.”
regions.goodToKnow: Henschke’s Hill of Grace, one of Australia’s most famous wines, is made here.

regions.name: MCLAREN VALE
regions.description: Mostly Shiraz in the rolling hills of the Fleurieu: dark and rich, with licorice, roast meat, mocha and graphite.

pairs.name: Braised Short Rib
pairs.why: McLaren Vale Shiraz with short rib.

regions.sayIt: “McLaren Vale: dark, rich Shiraz.”
regions.goodToKnow: Alcohol here can naturally reach 15–16%.

regions.name: COONAWARRA
regions.description: Coonawarra’s best Cabernet grows on dusty red clay, giving depth, powerful tannins and a subtle dried-herb quality.
regions.sayIt: “Coonawarra: Cabernet from red clay soil.”
regions.goodToKnow: Look for blackberry, black currant, cedar, spearmint and bay leaf.

regions.name: UCO VALLEY
regions.description: Some of Mendoza’s highest vineyards, known for elegant, age-worthy wines. Areas include Tupungato, Tunuyán and San Carlos.
regions.sayIt: “Uco Valley: high-altitude Malbec with elegance.”
regions.goodToKnow: Gualtallary, in Tupungato, is prized by collectors for its limestone soils.

regions.name: MARGARET RIVER
regions.description: Called the most isolated wine region in the world, three hours south of Perth. In about 50 years it became world class for Cabernet and Chardonnay.
regions.sayIt: “Margaret River: world-class Cabernet and Chardonnay, by the ocean.”
regions.goodToKnow: It’s phylloxera-free, and most vines grow on their own roots.

regions.name: HUNTER VALLEY
regions.description: Australia’s oldest working wine region, outside Sydney, known for both Shiraz and Sémillon.

pairs.name: Walleye Milanese
pairs.why: A lean white with fried fish.

regions.sayIt: “Hunter Valley: Australia’s oldest wine region.”
regions.goodToKnow: Its Sémillon tastes of lime, lilac, Asian pear and candle wax.

regions.name: YARRA VALLEY
regions.description: A mix of altitudes and soils gives very different wines, from Bordeaux-like Cabernet to Pinot Noir and delicate Chardonnay.
regions.sayIt: “Yarra Valley: cool, elegant Chardonnay and Pinot.”
regions.goodToKnow: It’s known for cult single-vineyard Nebbiolo too.

regions.name: CLARE VALLEY
regions.description: Arguably some of Australia’s finest dry Riesling, plus elegant, savory Cabernet.
regions.sayIt: “Clare Valley: some of Australia’s best dry Riesling.”
regions.goodToKnow: Its famous Riesling sites include Watervale and Polish Hill River.

regions.name: TASMANIA
regions.description: A new frontier for cool-climate Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and sparkling wine: lean and smoky, often with subtle mushroom notes.
regions.sayIt: “Tasmania: Australia’s cool-climate island.”
regions.goodToKnow: Tasmania is under 0.5% of Australia’s grape harvest.

regions.name: MARLBOROUGH
regions.description: Famous for Sauvignon Blanc and now world-class Pinot Noir. The Wairau Valley, Southern Valleys and Awatere Valley each give their own style.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN NEW ZEALAND
regions.sayIt: “Marlborough: the world’s favourite Sauvignon Blanc.”
regions.goodToKnow: Until the late 1990s, most Marlborough Pinot went into sparkling wine.

regions.name: CENTRAL OTAGO
regions.description: The world’s southernmost wine region, best known for Pinot Noir, with tightly structured Chardonnay too.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN NEW ZEALAND
regions.sayIt: “Central Otago: the world’s southernmost wine.”
regions.goodToKnow: Chardonnay here ripens at lower sugar but keeps high acidity.

regions.name: HAWKE’S BAY
regions.description: A warm, maritime region on the North Island’s east coast, arguably New Zealand’s most complete, from Bordeaux blends to coastal Chardonnay.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN NEW ZEALAND
regions.sayIt: “Hawke’s Bay: New Zealand’s warm red country.”
regions.goodToKnow: Gimblett Gravels, the premier area, sits 15 km from the Pacific.

regions.name: MARTINBOROUGH
regions.description: Chardonnay with bright stone fruit and a mineral core, alongside world-class Pinot Noir.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN NEW ZEALAND
regions.sayIt: “Martinborough: small, cool and serious about Pinot.”
regions.goodToKnow: The best Chardonnays keep improving with age.

regions.name: NORTH CANTERBURY
regions.description: One of the world’s best regions for true cool-climate Chardonnay: clean, ripe fruit with fresh acidity.
regions.siblingsTitle: WHERE IT SITS IN NEW ZEALAND
regions.sayIt: “North Canterbury: cool, clean Chardonnay.”
regions.goodToKnow: Limestone soils give the best wines elegance and minerality.

regions.name: LUJÁN DE CUYO
regions.description: Home to many modern wineries. Its Malbec leans to black fruit and Asian spice, with a dusty, graphite-like finish.
regions.sayIt: “Luján de Cuyo: Mendoza Malbec with black fruit and spice.”
regions.goodToKnow: Wines are often labelled by town: Agrelo, Vistalba, Las Compuertas, Perdriel.

regions.name: STELLENBOSCH
regions.description: South Africa’s most developed winelands and the centre of wine tourism, often compared to Napa.
regions.sayIt: “Stellenbosch: South Africa’s Napa.”
regions.goodToKnow: Top wines come from granite soils about 600 million years old.

regions.name: PATAGONIA
regions.description: An up-and-coming frontier in Argentine wine, with its own style of Pinot Noir from Neuquén and Río Negro.

taste.line: Pinot with sweet red fruit and herbal notes.

regions.sayIt: “Patagonia: Pinot Noir from the end of the world.”
regions.goodToKnow: Patagonian Pinot balances sweet red fruit with leafy, herbal tea notes.
